text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Streaming tail latency spike in eu-west-2 observed. p99 for streaming append ops > 6s, increased aborts for long-poll connections. Automatic routing fallback triggered for some customers. Investigating.

ravi.k: I'm on it — can someone grab quick customer impact numbers (tenants, error rate, affected routes)?

leah: p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 6.2s for streaming append over websocket. Error rate up 0.28% (from 0.01%). Affected: ~12 tenants, mostly on dedicated pools in eu-west-2a/2b. CPU/gpu look fine on serving hosts.

jamie: saw a bunch of SYN retransmits and TLS handshake timeouts in the region at the same times. Correlating with NAT gateway metrics, ephemeral port exhaustion looks suspicious.

olivia: do we have packet loss / retransmit metrics across AZs? Could be cross-AZ routing flaps.

network-bot: NetAlerts: increased TCP retransmits on eni-*-eu-west-2a -> eni-*-eu-west-2b path, packet_loss ~ 4-7% measured over 5m windows. DNS latencies also spiking (~200-800ms for internal service discovery).

matt: timeline: spike started 12:03UTC, peaked 12:11UTC, auto-fallbacks began 12:14UTC and reduced immediate 500 errors but tail remains.

ravi.k: OK. Initial plan: 1) mitigate customer impact (force-failover traffic to eu-west-3 for affected pools if capacity allows), 2) short-term network mitigations (increase NAT ephemeral ports / rotate NATs), 3) root-cause collection (pcaps, tcpdump, NAT metrics, BGP/route tables). Who can run the NAT port scale now?

leah: I can do NAT params. Suggest: bump ephemeral port allocation on relevant NGWs and create a temporary NAT replacement target group. Command (AWS example):
```
# example - do not paste directly into prod without review
aws ec2 modify-nat-gateway-attributes --nat-gateway-id ngw-0123456789abcdef --connectivity-type public
# then rotate or attach new ENIs, expand port range in iptables on ngw-proxies
```
I'll also flip DNS weight to prefer eu-west-3 for streaming-route.vpc.redwood.local for affected tenants.

jamie: I'll collect packet captures from a couple of streaming gateways and the NAT nodes. Running tcpdump for 120s: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream-spike.pcap -i any host <gateway-ip> and port 443`

network-bot: Note: provider reported intermittent cross-AZ link maintenance around 12:05-12:09UTC for eu-west-2; their bulletin lists BFD flaps on a subset of spine links.

olivia: Given provider maintenance, prefer region failover to eu-west-3 as primary mitigation. Can infra accept the shift for 12 tenants? We have warm capacity but need a controlled roll.

matt: Start canary failover for low-traffic tenants first. I'll kick off rollout script to reassign routing policy for 3 tenants now. If stable, continue in waves.

ravi.k: Do it. Also add `robin` label to this thread for oncall handoff later. Important: ensure we preserve request tracing headers for postmortem.

leah: Canary started at 12:32UTC for tenant A,B,C. So far p99 reduced to 320ms for those canary tenants. Performing bulk shift in 5m windows.

jamie: tcpdumps show repeated TLS handshake retransmits followed by long delays on initial SYN->ACK on some flows. Sequence: SYN, SYN+ACK delayed ~200-500ms, client retransmit -> handshake eventually succeeds or times out after 6s. This matches NAT ephem port reuse and connection queuing.

network-bot: New alert: NAT ephemeral ports nearing exhaustion on ngw-0a (80% in-use). Recommendation: rotate NAT target and increase ephemeral pool on proxies.

leah: I've rotated in standby NATs and increased proxy ephemeral range. Monitoring.

matt: Customer impact update: after region failover + NAT rotation, overall p99 for streaming reduced to ~700ms across affected tiers. Error rate down to 0.05%. Still some tail spikes for legacy routes pinned to older pools.

ravi.k: Good. Next actions: 1) finish migrating remaining tenants off the affected pools (in next 20 mins), 2) collect PCAPs + NAT logs + provider events for postmortem, 3) open incident JIRA and assign RCA. I'm handing ops over to night oncall (olivia) at 13:00UTC — leaving this thread for followups.

olivia: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring streaming tail and NAT port usage, plus coordinate with provider for link logs. If we see any regressions, @ravi.k please re-alert.

matt: noted — will attach metric snapshots and the temp playbook to the incident ticket.

ravi.k: Postmortem checklist (quick): timeline, customer-impact table, mitigations applied (region failover, NAT rotation, ephemeral pool increase), root cause hypothesis (provider cross-AZ link maintenance + NAT ephemeral exhaustion causing handshake queuing), follow-up actions (increase redundant NAT capacity, add synthetic streaming p99 alarms per AZ, provider remediation SLA discussion).

oncall-bot: Pager cleared. Incident status: mitigated -> degraded but stable. Please update incident ticket and set postmortem owner.

olivia: I'll own the postmortem and ping infra/network for followups. Leaving notes here and in the ticket. Closing active mitigation, leaving monitoring watch for 4h. :white_check_mark:
